editorialPurpose: Explain how corrected simultaneous local/reference solar-time readings transform into longitude, with a brief qualifiedH4 contribution.

narrativeStructure.label: Question
narrativeStructure.purpose: Recognize a timekeeper can assist an east–west navigation problem.

narrativeStructure.label: Reference
narrativeStructure.purpose: Understand the timekeeper carries time tied to somewhere known.

narrativeStructure.label: Local time and correction
narrativeStructure.purpose: Understand observation supplies local time and the solar observation must be corrected to a comparable basis.

narrativeStructure.label: Simultaneity
narrativeStructure.purpose: Understand this is a simultaneous spatial comparison rather than a ship journey lasting two hours.

narrativeStructure.label: Time becomes angle
narrativeStructure.purpose: Understand why different meridians have different local solar times and why the time gap maps to an angle.

narrativeStructure.label: Concrete readings
narrativeStructure.purpose: Understand12:00 reference and14:00 local are simultaneous comparable readings.

narrativeStructure.label: Longitude reveal
narrativeStructure.purpose: Understand local time ahead corresponds to east, and2×15° gives30°.

narrativeStructure.label: Historical engineering
narrativeStructure.purpose: Recognize Harrison’s important contribution without replacing the mechanism with biography.

narrativeStructure.label: Historical scope
narrativeStructure.purpose: Understand marine clocks did not erase other longitude approaches.

narrativeStructure.label: Payoff
narrativeStructure.purpose: Leave the viewer with the correct causal system.

segments.text: How can a clock tell a ship where it is?
By keeping the time at a known reference point.
Sailors use the Sun to find local time, corrected to match the clock’s timekeeping.
Compare them at the same moment.
Earth’s turning links that time difference to longitude: fifteen degrees per hour.
Twelve at the reference. Two in the afternoon locally.
Two hours ahead. Thirty degrees east.
Harrison’s H4 helped demonstrate accurate timekeeping at sea.
Other astronomical methods remained useful too.
The clock carries time. Observation and calculation reveal longitude.

storyAngle: Two simultaneous times become an east–west angle; the clock supplies reference time, not a position display.
